approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a bounded population of high-scoring accepted molecules, using connected-fragment crossover and ordinary mutations. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Before each batch it fits a Gaussian process to every accepted observation, using count-Morgan fingerprints and generalized Tanimoto similarity, fixed observation noise, and archive-based score normalization. It generates a larger pool of fresh valid unique offspring, draws correlated posterior functions over that pool, and emits the available maximum of each draw. Accepted scores update the archive and score-greedy survivor population. The residual amplitude currently comes entirely from the fitted posterior and inherited normalization; earlier forecast errors do not adjust its influence on selection.
approach.novelty: Add one task-local feedback rule for the amplitude of those existing correlated residuals. Save the prediction and raw allocation uncertainty before scoring each emitted molecule, then use only earlier accepted errors to estimate a bounded common multiplier, shrunk toward the inherited value of one. Large standardized errors receive a capped contribution to this estimator while remaining fully visible in diagnostics. The same multiplier scales the whole next draw without changing the fitted means or correlations. Completed siblings removed residual influence, correlation, count multiplicity, or crossover; this experiment retains them and tests whether their existing residual amplitude can usefully adapt. Historical noise-fitting controls changed GP regularization and lost endpoint score despite better prediction diagnostics, so complete endpoint comparisons remain decisive.

observed_bottleneck: The current count-GP Parent n-62daf219c70a has no accepted-error feedback into allocation amplitude. Its complete current-profile panel has mean endpoint 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. The matched removals support retaining sampled influence (n-299096e31fe7: mean delta -0.07686116167690966), correlation (n-54adc6a641e8: -0.018447481386582327), and count multiplicity (n-e00db808bbb4: -0.051295849138213355), but do not establish the inherited amplitude as optimal. These effects have task-seed exceptions and share one baseline. Mean-only allocation lowered its own selected-stream prediction MSE while losing endpoints; correlation removal increased some local improvement counts while losing endpoints. Historical count evidence n-559d25e9c9c7 and the current binary removal show that lower error can coexist with narrow, undercovered latent intervals. Historical binary/exchange-containing noise controls n-9002c3d22369 and n-e6bce5cb59ec improved selected-stream coverage/error but lost 0.01596063945276797 and 0.017540011331270994 mean endpoint score. In the latter, an initially flat archive preceded a large accepted score far outside even an inflated interval. These observations motivate testing amplitude feedback, not assuming that coverage is the cause of endpoint loss or that one multiplier will anticipate the first surprise. A read-only replay of the one fixed estimator below on all 435 Parent pools changed 354 batch sets with inherited first batches in all 15 streams; it reused Parent feedback and approximate reconstructed residuals, so it establishes potential exposure only.
hypothesis: Scale the existing correlated allocation residual by one bounded task-local multiplier learned from earlier accepted, pre-feedback standardized squared prediction errors, with shrinkage toward inherited amplitude one and no change to fitted count-GP means or cross-candidate correlation.

finding_summary.headline: Accepted-error scaling changes choices and intervals but lowers the matched endpoint mean by 0.038141
finding_summary.insights: This feedback-amplitude variant is an executed but unsuccessful endpoint intervention; it does not overturn the separate evidence for retaining nonzero correlated residuals. Changing interval coverage and many selected identities is insufficient to establish useful search or calibration away from the acquired stream. Shrinkage and capped contributions preserve bounded adaptation, but 382 large errors remain in the Child diagnostics, and a common multiplier cannot anticipate a first unseen surprise. One shared first-batch miss is 253 raw allocation SDs from its prediction while the multiplier is still one. Which changed choices produce the losses remains unresolved. Molecular evidence preserves conventional alternatives and some larger improving ring families alongside reactive bond environments, crowded geometry, excessive elaboration and fragments. Those mixed examples rule out a universal size, ring or heteroatom rule as the explanation for the score loss. The next scientific question is which conditions make amplitude changes useful; these results do not justify re-tuning the preregistered constants after seeing the panel or combining sibling effects.
finding_summary.results: The fixed feedback recurrence reconstructs for all 4,350 accepted emitted predictions and excludes the 150 initial observations. Emission multipliers range from 0.586 to 2.849, preserving the raw fitted model and cross-candidate correlation. Scaling changes 377 of 435 same-pool selected sets and creates 1703 strict same-mask winner disagreements. On the actual Child stream, nominal 95% coverage moves from 77.91% using raw jittered allocation SD to 90.69% using its prospectively scaled SD; the same saved means give identical MSE 0.011318. Coverage gains are not uniform. Mean endpoint score falls from 0.595670 to 0.557528, a paired loss of 0.038141 instead of the required gain of at least 0.002. All seed macros fall (-0.044258, -0.005456 and -0.064710), while eight task-seed endpoints improve and seven decline. The largest losses are deco_hop seed 0 (-0.248112) and sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 (-0.344354); median_2 improves in every seed.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles and bridged amines persist, with reactive substitutions, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This assessment reads all 4,500 Child observations, including 4,350 optimizer proposals, and all 4,500 observations in the fifteen published Parent trajectories named by the immutable request. Every supplied task and Search Seed 0, 1 and 2 is covered; no listed path is missing. The brief reports complete Child evaluation and complete profile-matched pairing to n-62daf219c70a under the Research in Depth epoch-1 profile, 300 observations per task and batches of ten. The chemistry spans aryl carbonyl and thiocarbonyl systems, methoxy-substituted cyclic hydrazones, nitroso-substituted azaarenes, bridged aryl amines, large nitrogen/carbonyl ring assemblies, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Small fragments and overgrown assemblies coexist with these leading families. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with substantial elaboration of a recurring family within individual trajectories; this is not global scaffold collapse. Proposal aromatic-string incidence ranges from 0.8391 to 0.9931 and ring-digit incidence from 0.8690 to 0.9943. These support abundant ring-containing and aromatic-labelled output, but do not measure aromatic stability, independent scaffolds or feasible three-dimensional geometry. Every task has charge-string and stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, despite visible aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic ring junctions. Recognizable medicinal functional groups coexist with direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, halomethyl groups, unusual sulfur environments, small unsaturated rings and crowded bridges; makeability and overall drug-likeness therefore remain questionable and weak, respectively, rather than uniformly absent. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts read from the supplied SMILES, not computed conformational, synthesis or property measurements. Parent endpoint and chemical comparisons are descriptive; they neither identify activation of residual-scale calibration nor attribute a chemical liability to that component. The last emitted molecule is distinguished from the retained highest-scoring observation.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 25, 26 and 24 heavy-atom tokens. Seed 0 combines an N-fluorinated pyrrolic ring and a pyridyl ketone/imine region with a small, multiply unsaturated carbocycle. Seed 1 instead makes a methoxy-substituted cyclic hydrazone carrying a thiourea-like carbonyl analogue, an N-chloromethyl substituent and a fluorophenyl group, with a crowded spiro/bridged unsaturated carbocyclic extension. Its chlorine is attached to carbon in the chloromethyl group, not directly to nitrogen. Seed 2 uses an arene annulated to small nitrogen rings, an N-ethyl substituent, methoxy substitution and an N-fluoro carboxanilide. Conventional indole carboxanilides are present among the initial observations. The proposal halogen-string incidence is 0.9241 and mean SMILES length 43.3, but many late leaders replace conventional connectivity with strained-looking ring arrangements or reactive substitutions.
liabilities: Direct N-F and N-Cl bonds occur in some families; the seed-1 leader instead carries N-chloromethyl functionality and a crowded carbocyclic bridge. These are distinct chemical concerns.
Multiple unsaturated small-ring junctions raise strain and synthetic-accessibility questions that SMILES validity and aromatic labels do not answer.
Potential stereogenic saturated junctions lack explicit stereochemical identity.
missing_features: The favored aryl/polar organization is present, but stereochemically defined and geometrically credible alternatives to the crowded spiro, bridged and small unsaturated ring arrangements are not demonstrated at the leading scores.

Conventional bond environments are not preserved consistently around the nitrogen and carbonyl regions; the observed nonfluorinated amide counterpart shows that the local N-F bond is dispensable in one scored context.
Independent plausible alternatives within each leading family remain limited, although the distinct families across seeds rule out an inability to change scaffolds.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders reach 0.4443186615775074, 0.4565130794320982 and 0.44049061101245846. Intact aryl/polar-ring organization is associated with useful scores: sulfur alone scores 0.0, while a much larger, multiply linked aryl ketone assembly at seed 0/evaluation 205 scores only 5.051687510283091e-18. Neither fragmentation nor general enlargement reproduces the leaders. Two close counterexamples narrow the reading: changing N-chloromethyl to N-fluoromethyl in the same seed-1 framework leaves the score at 0.4384465600248538; removing fluorine from the seed-2 amide nitrogen raises 0.4013778137849945 to 0.4031937733859023 while the N-chlorinated ring remains. These comparisons do not establish a universal benefit for direct N-halogenation. Matched Parent endpoints are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081: the Child has two gains and one loss while reaching different ring and carbonyl arrangements. No single missing target motif is identifiable from these trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader is a 27-atom fused nitrogen-rich dione with an N-acetyl group, a short ring bridge and a fluorinated fused azaarene. Seed 1 grows a 44-atom assembly of two substituted azaaryl carbonyl/oxygen ring systems linked through a phenylene/ether region; it includes carbon-bound fluoromethyl groups and a chloromethyl ether. Seed 2 reaches a 31-atom pair of azaarenes joined through an amino-substituted fluorinated carbon, with two carbon-bound nitroso groups, an N-bromo methylamino substituent and an N-chloromethyl vinylamino substituent. The N=O groups in that leader are nitroso groups, not nitro groups. A near leader also contains direct N-Cl and O-F bonds. Proposal aromatic-string incidence is 0.9724, ring-digit incidence 0.9736 and mean SMILES length 57.3. Familiar heteroaryl and carbonyl units are plentiful, but their decoration does not consistently resemble stable ordinary medicinal chemistry.
liabilities: Direct N-Br, N-Cl and O-F bonds, chloromethyl substitution and multiple nitroso groups warrant environment-specific reactivity assessment; they are not interchangeable with conventional aryl halides.
Large multiply decorated heteroaromatic assemblies and fused ring bridges create synthesis and conformational questions.
The fluorinated tetrahedral linker in the seed-2 family has no assigned stereochemistry.
missing_features: The output has abundant aromatic substitution and heterocyclic carbonyl groups; the remaining structural gap is consistent access to stable bond environments that retain their favorable organization, rather than a lack of rings or halogens.
The record does not establish a chemically independent, more accessible counterpart to the highly decorated nitroso/halogen family at its exact leading score.
Controlled elaboration is incomplete: duplication produces a much larger leading assembly without establishing a substantial score advantage over the more compact matched Parent family.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623, an optimizer-proposed smaller nitrogen/carbonyl ring assembly scores 0.50371777924653, and isolated F scores the observed floor of 0.5. The three seed leaders score 0.608035843329961, 0.6250172200027552 and 0.6331203407880724, associating the upper range with organized substituted aromatic frameworks rather than halogen atoms alone. In a directly comparable seed-1 pair, chloromethoxy and methoxy variants both score 0.6187363834422658, so that reactive chloromethyl ether adds no observed reward in this context. The Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. The substantial seed-0 decrease accompanies replacement of its Parent thione/halomethyl/O-F-containing family by the Child dione family; multiple structural changes preclude attributing the decrease to any one group. Seeds 1 and 2 provide positive endpoint counterexamples, with the 44-atom seed-1 leader barely above the 32-atom Parent leader. Extra size and reactive substitution are not universally productive.

per_task.generated_character: The 28-atom seed-0 leader contains a fused N-methyl cyclic amine/aminal region attached through a tertiary amine and ethylene segment to a dichlorinated arene bearing an aniline and an aminopropyl chain. The 31-atom seed-1 leader combines two substituted arenes, a fused small-ring amine and an unusual amino-substituted hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre written [SH](N), plus chloromethyl and fluoro substitution. The 28-atom seed-2 leader is a multiply bridged tertiary/secondary cyclic amine with two chlorinated aromatic regions, a phenol and an aryl ether bridge. Its chlorines are carbon-bound; it has no direct N- or O-halogen bond. A 29-atom relative also uses recognizable aryl ether and cyclic-amine functional groups. These are genuine basic-nitrogen-containing outputs, not an amine-deficient collection. Proposal halogen-string incidence is 0.9747 and mean SMILES length 53.3. The functional groups in seeds 0 and 2 are comparatively conventional, while their connected ring geometry and stereochemistry still require scrutiny.
liabilities: The multiply bridged seed-2 topology and fused small nitrogen rings in other examples raise synthesis and ring-geometry questions despite recognizable functional groups.
The seed-1 amino-substituted hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre and chloromethyl substituent warrant particular stability scrutiny.
Heavy halogenation and aromatic surface area are common, but solubility and selectivity are not measured by the displayed molecular scores.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical and conformational identities are missing for the successful bridged and saturated cyclic-amine frameworks.

A comparably evaluated conventional sulfur replacement is not established for the unusual seed-1 [SH](N) environment; high-scoring sulfur-free leaders show that this environment is not a universal requirement.
Protonation states are not explicitly resolved in the neutral SMILES. That is a state-representation limitation, not evidence that basic centres are absent or that another amine must be added.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197 and a substituted aryl ester without an available aliphatic amine scores 0.00035083244031306317. The seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders score 0.9884488865564339, 0.9468705717973529 and 0.9999915466069236; a second bridged aryl-amine structure reaches 0.9965963113396393. The visible association is the presentation of available aliphatic amines together with aromatic regions, not total nitrogen or halogen count. Presence of those regions is insufficient by itself: the final seed-0 proposal retains an aryl/amine assembly but scores 0.2542362051792611. Parent endpoints are 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012 in flexible or saturated cyclic-amine families. The Child seed-2 bridged structure nearly reproduces the corresponding endpoint while the other seeds finish lower. These scores are not measurements of synthetic accessibility, receptor selectivity or geometric realism, and no causal explanation for the changes follows from chemistry alone.

per_task.generated_character: The three seed leaders contain 36, 36 and 37 heavy-atom tokens, compared with 34, 32 and 29 in their matched Parent leaders. Seed 0 has two aryl regions joined into a crowded partially unsaturated nitrogen/dicarbonyl polycycle, with propyl, ethoxy and ether-containing ring segments. Seed 1 forms an extended aromatic-labelled fused system linked to a bridged lactam/ketone region and N-methyl amine. Seed 2 retains a propylquinoline joined through a larger nitrogen-containing lactam/amine ring to an ethyl-substituted arene with a fused lactone. That last family contains recognizable quinoline, amine, amide and lactone chemistry; it is not merely an exotic heteroatom string. Proposal ring-digit incidence is 0.9943, aromatic-string incidence 0.9931 and mean SMILES length 58.8. Halogen incidence is only 0.1253, showing that heavily halogenated chemistry is not common to every search. Ring assembly and geometry, rather than lack of rings, limit confidence in makeability.
liabilities: Crowded fused and bridged ring systems combine large aromatic regions with saturated nitrogen/carbonyl closures, creating substantial route and geometry questions.
A higher score accompanies some more elaborate structures without establishing their synthetic accessibility; the Parent and Child both retain this limitation.
The coexistence of nearly tied ring variants and much poorer large assemblies cautions against interpreting atom count as chemical progress.
missing_features: The favored aromatic, nitrogen and carbonyl combination is present, but simpler and demonstrably feasible connectivities preserving it at the leading scores are not established.
Saturated bridge and junction stereochemistry remains unspecified, and aromatic-labelled extended rings lack demonstrated conformational identity.

Chemically independent plausible alternatives within the leading series remain limited; distinct seed families and the recognizable lactone-containing family are counterexamples to total scaffold collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329; a much larger multiply linked nitrogen/carbonyl assembly at seed 0/evaluation 29 scores 0.11194341570991125 and methane scores 0.0. The three leaders reach 0.237857360478159, 0.2500935353730046 and 0.22997151900267843. Each exceeds its matched Parent endpoint of 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. This is a clear counterexample to treating all additional ring elaboration or all Child chemistry as score-worsening. Closely related ring arrangements also score well: the seed-0 shortened ring segment gives 0.23636929864965447 and the seed-1 rearranged fused framework gives 0.24970570913871912. A larger 39-atom seed-2 relative with an added carbon and nitrogen scores 0.2240996957501455, below its 37-atom leader; multiple changes prevent attribution to either atom alone. Reward is associated with the combined aromatic and nitrogen/carbonyl organization, not monotonically with molecular size or one unique bridge. The modest upper range does not identify a missing target structure.

per_task.generated_character: The 26-atom seed-0 leader combines a terminal alkyne and conjugated fluoroenol/diene side chain with a partly saturated fused imino/carbonyl nitrogen heterocycle, N-methyl substitution and a direct N-F bond. Its high unsaturation is not the same geometry as the Parent seed-2 small cyclic cumulene. The 27-atom seed-1 leader contains a methylhydrazino/thiocarbonyl chain, an N-F bond, an aldehyde, a small aromatic-labelled N-N-containing ring, a pyrrole and a fluorophenol. The 25-atom seed-2 leader is a fused dione bearing N-methyl, a chlorofluoroalkyl chain and an amino-substituted methylene-bridged arene; it has carbon-bound halogens without direct N-F. Proposal aromatic and ring-digit incidences are 0.8391 and 0.8690, below those of the other supplied tasks, and cumulated-double-bond incidence is 0.0529. These counters describe proposal strings, not validated aromaticity or a universal cyclic-cumulene requirement. The set also contains tiny fragments and much larger duplicated heterocyclic assemblies.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonds, hydrazino/thiourea-like linkages and an aldehyde coexist with highly unsaturated enolic chains; stability and tautomer identity remain uncharacterized.
Small aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings, crowded fused junctions and methylene-bridged arenes raise geometric and synthetic-accessibility concerns.
Very low-scoring overgrown and fragmented proposals show loss of useful molecular context, but do not justify a fixed molecular-size cutoff.
missing_features: Chemically stable and geometrically credible alternatives preserving the favorable compact fluorinated/polar context are not consistently demonstrated across seeds.

Assigned alkene and saturated-centre stereochemistry and established tautomeric identity are absent from the cited unsaturated and fused frameworks; the scores do not resolve those molecular-state questions.

The output does not establish that more fluorine or more direct N-F bonds supply the missing reward; both carbon-bound-only halogenated leaders and the local N-methyl counterexample limit that inference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298, the large duplicated aryl/dione assembly at seed 2/evaluation 24 scores 6.514810568357986e-29, and isolated F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26. The seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 leaders reach 0.6271099158041069, 0.4985562442855517 and 0.3765316086870727, associating useful scores with compact fluorinated/polar organization rather than fluorination or heterocycle count alone. Reconnecting the seed-0 leader's rings while retaining 26 atoms gives 0.524091160459897, demonstrating topology sensitivity without isolating a single bond effect. A closer counterexample changes one N-F substituent to N-methyl in a fixed fluorinated heterocycle/side-chain framework: 0.3859300919215334 becomes 0.4880748335956676. Thus direct N-F is not uniformly advantageous. Parent endpoints are 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. Seed 1 is a positive Child counterexample; seed 2 falls substantially while leaving the Parent cyclic-cumulene family for a different, still geometrically questionable bridged-arene family. Its final emitted molecule scores 0.13971951248650405, distinct from its retained 0.3765316086870727 incumbent. The data do not identify a missing target pharmacophore or prove that the Parent's doubtful geometry caused its higher score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c through the identical-chemistry baseline n-62daf219c70a, and is re-observed in n-38bcd7569cce on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and batches of ten. Current leaders contain direct N-F or N-Br, chloromethyl groups, nitroso functionality or unusual amino-substituted sulfur; a near leader has O-F and N-Cl. Current scored counterexamples constrain the gap: removing an amide N-F bond changes 0.4013778137849945 to 0.4031937733859023, replacing chloromethoxy with methoxy leaves 0.6187363834422658 unchanged, and replacing a ring N-F substituent with N-methyl changes 0.3859300919215334 to 0.4880748335956676. A bridged aryl amine reaches 0.9999915466069236 with carbon-bound halogens and no direct N/O-halogen bond. These are local chemical associations, not component attribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments while retaining favorable aromatic and heterocyclic organization.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Transformations should distinguish bond environment from element identity and offer conventional local alternatives while preserving useful relationships learned from accepted task-local scores. Retain ordinary carbon-bound halogens and available amines where appropriate. The missing capability is reliable context-sensitive chemistry, not a universal prohibition of nitrogen, sulfur, halogens or all reactive groups; no blanket filter's score benefit is established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This geometry gap originates in the n-c55c3d520a2c assessment reproduced by n-62daf219c70a; the current complete, matched three-seed panel supplies new spiro/bridged hydrazones, multiply unsaturated small carbocycles, densely connected aryl amines, extended aromatic-labelled systems and large nitrogen/carbonyl ring closures. High ring-digit and aromatic-string incidences do not establish feasible geometry. Counterexamples include conventional initial aromatic carboxamides and recognizable amine, lactam and lactone motifs. Some current more elaborate nitrogen/carbonyl ring families exceed their matched Parent endpoints, and a bridged amine nearly reaches the supplied score ceiling. Thus the concern is unresolved feasibility, not proof that bridges, ring richness or elaboration always reduce score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish ring graphs that can be written from geometrically credible fused, bridged and unsaturated structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need sensitivity to size, bridge connectivity and unsaturation geometry, together with alternative feasible connectivities preserving learned favorable functional arrangements. A chemically credible alternative should be evaluated in its own task-local context. Ring counts, aromatic labels and high objective scores alone cannot establish synthesis or conformational plausibility; this assessment supplies no causal score benefit for a geometry rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This identity gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a; it persists in the current matched Search panel at the same observation budget and cadence. Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0 for every task despite substituted saturated, spiro and bridged environments in the cited leaders. Explicit charge incidence is also 0.0, but available aliphatic amines are plainly present, so charge-free notation cannot diagnose missing basic centres. The record establishes unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical or protonation-related score penalty.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity when new potentially stereogenic saturated centres and ring junctions are generated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry when a generated constitution requires it, with appropriate exceptions for achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Treat protonation, tautomerism and alkene geometry as separate state questions. No particular stereoisomer, charge state, objective-specific structure or component-specific failure is justified by the available scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This context-control gap is inherited from n-c55c3d520a2c via n-62daf219c70a and has fresh evidence in the current three-seed, 300-observation panel. Tiny halogen or hydrocarbon proposals reach observed floors, including late proposals, while some large duplicated aryl/heterocyclic assemblies score far below more compact leaders. A 44-atom decorated family barely exceeds its 32-atom matched Parent leader. The counterexamples matter: all three leading nitrogen/carbonyl ring assemblies are larger than their matched Parents and have higher endpoints, while several compact amine families already score highly. Neither universal shrinking nor universal growth follows from these observations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve useful functional-group context while controlling fragmentation and excessive scaffold elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to retain useful combinations of aromatic, amine and carbonyl regions while offering controlled simplification, replacement and independent feasible scaffold alternatives. The capability gap is consistent preservation of productive molecular context, not inability to make small or large molecules. Avoid a fixed size floor, a universal growth preference or claims that additional diversity must improve score; chemistry associations do not isolate the residual-scale intervention.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only task-local archive, bounded greedy survivors and score-quantile parent selection.

Connected-fragment crossover, optional post-crossover mutation, ordinary mutation continuation and all seven ordinary atom/bond/ring operations with fixed probabilities and bounded retry/saturation rules.
Disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange with passive opportunity tracing; stable canonical/isomeric identity, original graph reuse and both duplicate scopes.
Count-Morgan shared features and cache, generalized Tanimoto GP, original normalization and observation noise, full joint covariance, full Cholesky/jitter and raw next-fit probes.
Nonzero correlated residual allocation with inherited base normals, stable masks/ties and identity-bound saved predictions, now under one positive accepted-error amplitude multiplier.
Fixed surplus pools, batches, budget/profile, fresh task state, finite guards and original valid-pool numerical fallback.
